name: blue-man
role: THE LOCKED REFERENCE — the recurring character every ai-video shot drives from
rule: NEVER generate this character from text twice. Every still that needs him is gen_image.py --ref character.png; every clip is image-to-video from a frame that already contains him. Re-deriving him from the prompt is a bug.

design.body: matte clay-like cobalt blue, smooth rounded simplified forms, minimalist 3D sculpture
design.head: completely smooth and featureless — no eyes, no mouth, no ears, no hair
design.accessory: exactly ONE: chunky mustard-yellow knit scarf around the neck (his identity marker — must appear in every shot)
design.proportions: childlike ~4 heads tall, oversized rounded head, mitten hands, stubby legs, no neck taper

generation.prompt: A single stylized faceless humanoid character, full body, standing centered in a relaxed neutral pose, arms at his sides, front view. His body is matte clay-like cobalt blue with smooth rounded simplified forms, like a high-quality minimalist low-poly sculpture. His head is completely smooth and featureless - no eyes, no mouth, no ears, no hair. He wears exactly one accessory: a chunky mustard-yellow knit scarf around his neck. Soft diffused studio lighting, gentle ambient occlusion, plain warm pale-grey seamless studio backdrop, soft contact shadow under his feet. Minimalist 3D render, clean silhouette, high quality, no text, no watermark.

shot_workflow: 1. start frame: gen_image.py --ref ai-shorts/blue-man/character.png --prompt '<the same faceless blue clay character with his mustard scarf, in SCENE...>' -> shots/NN-slug.png
2. clip: image-to-video from that start frame (gen_clip.py --set image_url=... or bakeoff_clip.py --ref ...)
3. loop shots: models with an end-frame input (seedance end_image_url, kling tail_image_url) get the SAME frame as start and end — frame 0 == last frame is a constraint we hand the model, not luck
